title: Epoched transactional resume semantics and SDK interop for Python/TS/Go
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: PRD to define a cross-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) specification for resumable streaming and paginated fetches that supports transactional semantics across model fanout and ensures deterministic idempotency. Focus areas: epoched cursors with lease/ttl, resume tokens that encode epoch+offset+idempotency, conflict detection for multi-writer scenarios, and clear downgrade/migration behavior for older SDKs.
goals: Define a single resume token format that all SDKs can generate/consume
Guarantee monotonic ordering and detect epoch mismatches to avoid duplication on resume
Document downgrade behavior for older clients and provide a migration plan
Provide deterministic acceptance tests that QA and SDK teams can run across languages
Ensure server and client-side backoff and retry policies interact safely with resume semantics
scope_inclusions: Resume token spec and validation rules
Lexicon for epoch, lease TTL, offset, and idempotency fields
SDK changes in Python, TS, and Go to expose resume/resume_if_valid APIs
Server-side compatibility checks and fallbacks to stateless cursors when necessary
End-to-end test matrix and CI jobs for interop tests
scope_exclusions: Full redesign of existing pagination APIs (we will extend current patterns)
Changes to the persisted storage model beyond visible resume metadata
Billing/usage model changes related to resumed requests
decision_log: 2026-02-21: Chose compact base64 token containing {version, epoch, offset, id_token, sig} to balance cross-language parsing and forward compatibility
2026-02-27: Agreed on lease TTL default 5m with server-override header for high-availability customers
2026-03-03: Opted for client-exposed 'resume_if_epoch_matches(token)' method rather than silent fallback to stateless fetch to avoid implicit duplicates
2026-03-09: Decided to include a migration header 'X-RW-Resume-Version' to opt older servers/clients into safe-mode behavior
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Resume token round-trip: Create a stream in Python, capture token after N events, disconnect, reconnect in TS using token -> must resume at offset N without duplicates
AC-2: Epoch mismatch handling: If token epoch < server epoch by >1, server returns EXPIRED_EPOCH and client surfaces a RewindRequired error; client must not deduplicate silently
AC-3: Lease expiry: If resume occurs after lease TTL, server rejects resume and returns RESUME_TTL_EXPIRED; SDKs show clear guidance and automatic fallback option in docs

AC-4: Multi-writer conflict: When two parallel consumers attempt resume with same token and server detects conflicting transactions, one gets conflict error and diagnostics header with 'conflict_epoch'
AC-5: Backoff interplay: A reconnect triggered by transient 5xx must obey exponential backoff and preserve resume token; at 429, client should jitter and preserve token as well
AC-6: Interop CI: Cross-language e2e test matrix (Python/TS/Go permutations) runs in CI and passes in >95% of randomized reconnect scenarios before merge
test_matrix: Matrix axes: SDK language (py/ts/go), network loss window (100ms/1s/10s), lease TTL (default/short/long), server epoch bump (none/1/2)
Include deterministic seed for event generation so test failures are reproducible
Add fuzz case: truncated token, corrupted signature -> server returns INVALID_TOKEN and client surfaces user-friendly error
migration_and_compatibility_plan: Phase 1 (opt-in): Add ResumeVersion header and new resume token format behind feature flag for internal customers
Phase 2 (grace): SDKs include dual-parsers: try new token format, fall back to legacy cursor transparently for reads only
Phase 3 (enforce): After 90 days, servers may reject legacy resume tokens with deprecation header; provide telemetry to owners
Provide compatibility shim in TS SDK for older Node runtimes that lack stable WebCrypto APIs (use HMAC fallback with safe defaults)
developer_contracts: Token format: base64v1 -> JSON fields: v:int, e:bigint, o:int, id:uuid, s:hmac(hex) encoded and base64-urlsafe
Client API: resume(token) -> Stream; resume_if_epoch_matches(token, expected_epoch) -> Stream or explicit ResumeEpochMismatch error
Error taxonomy: INVALID_TOKEN, RESUME_TTL_EXPIRED, EXPIRED_EPOCH, CONFLICTING_TRANSACTION, TRANSIENT_SERVER_ERROR
Telemetry: SDKs must emit resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_failure.reason with normalized tags
open_questions: Q1: Should the token be opaque to clients or allow clients to read epoch for optimistic routing? (Decision leaned toward readable epoch field)
Q2: How do we expose automatic checkpointing in languages with weak background-thread guarantees (Go/Node)? Proposing explicit flush() semantics
Q3: Do we support batched resume across model fanout (single token resuming multiple model shards)? Needs engineering validation for atomicity
qa_plan: Create interop jobs that run every PR in 'sdk-interop' pipeline
Add synthetic production-like replay test to canary environment simulating 2000 concurrent streams with randomized disconnects
Establish release gating: all three SDK e2e matrices must be green and flakiness <3% over 24h before release
rollout_strategy: Start with internal alpha customers and feature-flag on runtime for Dedicated clusters
Gradual rollout over 4 weeks with telemetry monitoring for resume_failure rates
Automated rollback if client-facing resume_failure rate exceeds 0.5% in production for 1h
